params.body:
Reports were the one kind of content that never passed editorial. The calendar
lived in a seeder on the public site and the PDF arrived through
`php artisan gentells:report` run over ssh, so publishing one needed a
developer, which is exactly what that command's own docblock says it wanted to
avoid.

It also put the rasterising on the wrong machine. The public site holds a copy
of what editorial released and shows it; turning 24MB of PDF into preview
images is work, and work belongs on the side that does the work. Because it sat
over there it needed poppler on a box Forge does not provision, and that only
surfaced when a report had to go out: the command stopped on `pdftoppm
ontbreekt` and the machine has no sudo to fix it.

## What moves here

- **`reports` table + `reports-store`** — the calendar, plus the fingerprint of
  whatever file is on disk. Availability is deliberately **not** stored:
  `status` carries Maarten's announcement and runs ahead of reality, so the far
  side derives what it can actually deliver from the file it holds. R2 stood at
  "available, with preview" for weeks with no PDF and no pages.
- **`report-render`** — `pdftoppm` to jpeg, `sharp` to webp. Only the released
  pages are rendered, because what is never rendered can never be served by
  accident.
- **Studio routes** — list, amend, upload, drop, and preview a page.
- **Projection endpoints** — `/internal/projection/reports` plus `/file` and
  `/preview/:n`, so the site can pull metadata and binaries and skip a 24MB
  download it already has.
- **`multipart.mjs`** — the parser the cover upload had inline, now in one
  place. Two copies is how one of them keeps a bug the other fixed, and this one
  has a trailing-CRLF subtlety worth having once.

## Dependencies are declared, not assumed

`sharp` ships its own binary and goes in `package.json`. `poppler-utils` cannot,
so CI installs it and the render test **fails** without it rather than skipping.
That gap is what caused this in the first place.

## Migration

`bin/seed-reports.mjs` moves the seven calendar rows across once and leaves
alone anything already here: the script is the move, not the truth.

Follow-ups in their own PRs: the Studio gains a Reports section, and the site
pulls reports through the projection and drops `IngestReport`.

## Tests

712 pass (was 698). 14 new across `reports-store` and `report-render`, the
latter against a PDF the test builds itself rather than a binary fixture nobody
can read.
params.title: Reports belong in the Studio, not in an artisan command
